failures.rule: brand/constitution.md E1, E2 and Article 1.4; product/ui-constitution.md Article 7
failures.place: Both screens: thick white arcs in the upper-right corner and beneath the jacket beside the primary action
failures.issue: The high-contrast stripes become prominent graphic shapes, competing with the jacket, price and action. Texture is permitted, but this strength gives the brand decoration attention that E1 reserves for the item and money. This is a visual judgment about the shown result, not a ban on the open Strong lines option.

across_options.issue: The placement comparison also changes texture: the baseline has faint arcs; Header band has no discernible deliberate texture; Whole moment retains faint arcs on the offer but loses them on Sold. This confounds D5's Where comparison with its Texture comparison (brand/constitution.md Article 14.4).

The item photographs are not pixel-stable across options. Jacket folds, pocket detail and wood grain subtly change in sharpness and shape, especially in the texture variants. Image content is outside the field decision and should not be treated as evidence for that decision (brand/constitution.md Article 14.4).

Review limits: this is a raster-image review. Type-size and margin findings are visual estimates normalized to a 390-wide phone, not computed CSS measurements. Part IV explicitly makes B13, B15, B22 and B27 not applicable without source. Hidden More-menu contents and interactions cannot be verified. Article 13 was checked for visible tells; no three-axis default-test failure is asserted without a comparative default artifact. Board callouts, the connecting arrow and the dotted arc were treated as annotations, not app UI. D5 expressly opens broader color coverage, so exceeding one third would not itself disqualify that option. No new designs are proposed.
